high.title: T-bill Yields Mixed as Central Bank Stays Hawkish
high.summary: The Bureau of the Treasury (BTr) achieved a full award of its P50 billion T-bill offering, with total tenders reaching P126.091 billion — more than twice the amount on offer, though slightly below the previous auction's P136.841 billion in bids. Yields came in mixed, reflecting the market's attempt to price in continued hawkish signals from the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) alongside heightened geopolitical risk stemming from renewed US-Iran hostilities. The strong bid-to-cover ratio signals that domestic liquidity remains ample and investor appetite for short-duration government paper is resilient. However, the mixed yield outcome suggests some divergence in rate expectations at different tenors — traders are likely pricing in a "higher for longer" BSP stance at the short end, while geopolitical uncertainty may be compressing risk appetite at the longer end. **Key watch points:** Any shift in BSP forward guidance, the trajectory of US-Iran tensions (which could drive oil prices and import costs higher, pressuring PHP and inflation), and next week's T-bond auction results for signals on longer-duration sentiment.

high.title: Peso Weakens on Middle East Clashes
high.summary: The Philippine peso depreciated 8.4 centavos to close at P61.599 per dollar on Monday, down from Friday's P61.515 close, as renewed US-Iran military exchanges triggered broad risk-off sentiment and safe-haven USD demand. The peso opened the session weaker at P61.61 before recovering intraday to P61.56, highlighting two-way volatility but an overall bearish bias for the local currency. The Middle East escalation introduces a key macro risk for PHP on multiple fronts: (1) **Oil price upside** — the Philippines is a net oil importer, and higher crude prices would widen the trade deficit and increase import-driven inflation, both of which are structurally negative for the peso; (2) **Risk-off USD strength** — broad dollar demand during geopolitical flare-ups typically pressures EM FX including PHP; (3) **BSP intervention risk** — if the peso approaches key psychological levels (e.g., P62.00), the BSP may intervene via spot or forward USD sales. **Key watch points:** Direction of Brent crude, US-Iran ceasefire prospects, BSP verbal or market intervention signals, and whether the peso can stabilize sub-P61.60 in Tuesday's session.

high.title: Two More 25-bp Rate Hikes Seen This Year
high.summary: Deutsche Bank Research is forecasting two additional 25-basis-point rate hikes by the BSP at its August 27 and October 22 policy meetings, citing broadening price pressures despite a modest easing in headline inflation. June headline CPI slowed to a three-month low of 6.4%, but core inflation — which excludes volatile food and energy components — remains elevated and continues to widen, signaling that underlying demand-driven pressures have not yet been tamed. This hawkish outlook carries significant implications across all three asset classes. For PHP/USD, further tightening could provide short-term support to the peso by attracting yield-seeking capital inflows and narrowing the interest rate differential with the Fed. For Philippine government bonds, the prospect of higher policy rates is bearish for duration — expect upward pressure on yields across the curve, particularly at the short-to-medium end. PSEi could face headwinds as higher borrowing costs compress equity valuations and dampen domestic consumption. Traders should closely monitor the August 27 BSP meeting for forward guidance and watch core inflation prints as the key policy trigger.

high.title: T-Bill and Bond Rates May Be Mixed as Conflict Weighs
high.summary: The Bureau of the Treasury (BTr) is set to auction P50 billion in T-bills (P20 billion each in 91- and 182-day tenors; P10 billion in 364-day) on Monday, followed by a P30 billion reissuance of 10-year T-bonds on Tuesday. Market participants are navigating a complex backdrop: renewed Middle East conflict is driving risk-off sentiment globally, while hawkish BSP signals are reinforcing upward pressure on the short end of the curve. The mixed rate outlook reflects a tug-of-war between safe-haven demand for government paper and the rate hike premium being priced in. For bond investors, the 10-year auction will be a critical gauge of appetite for duration amid the tightening cycle. Elevated auction cut-off rates could signal further curve steepening. Watch auction bid-to-cover ratios and cut-off yields as real-time indicators of market sentiment on both BSP policy and geopolitical risk tolerance.

high.title: Season of Selling to End Philippine Peso Rally, Strategists Say
high.summary:
The Philippine peso's recent relief rally — triggered by the initial US-Iran ceasefire — is expected to be short-lived, with strategists warning of renewed downside pressure driven by structural seasonal factors. Historical Bloomberg data shows the peso has weakened an average of **1.6% against the USD in Q3** over the past decade, making it the currency's worst-performing quarter of the year. The primary driver is **corporate dollar buying**: local companies front-load import payments ahead of the year-end peak consumption season, creating persistent USD demand that pressures the peso. For FX traders, this seasonal pattern represents a high-conviction directional signal — any near-term peso strength should be viewed as a selling opportunity rather than a trend reversal. Bond investors should also take note, as renewed PHP weakness could complicate the BSP's rate-cutting calculus, potentially keeping yields elevated at the longer end of the curve. Key risks to watch: pace of geopolitical re-escalation between the US and Iran, BSP FX intervention activity, and the trajectory of import demand data heading into Q3.

---

medium.title: Banks Could Face Sanctions Under Financial Consumer Protection Law
medium.summary: The BSP has released a draft circular implementing Republic Act No. 11765 (Financial Products and Services Consumer Protection Act), outlining a regulatory framework that could expose banks and financial institutions to administrative sanctions, penalties, stop orders, or suspension for non-compliance. While primarily a consumer protection measure, this development is relevant for banking sector investors as it introduces incremental compliance costs and operational risk for Philippine banks. Stricter enforcement could affect earnings of listed banking names on the PSEi, particularly those with large retail banking franchises. Fund managers with exposure to Philippine bank equities should monitor the final circular's scope and timeline for implementation.

medium.title: LANDBANK Plans Sustainability Bond Issuance
medium.summary: State-run Land Bank of the Philippines (LANDBANK) is planning a peso-denominated sustainability bond offering of at least P5 billion early next year. The issuance adds to a growing pipeline of ESG-themed peso bonds in the local market, which could absorb domestic liquidity and provide incremental supply to the Philippine bond market. While the size is modest, the timing and pricing of this issuance — when announced — will serve as a useful market signal on institutional appetite for quasi-sovereign paper and prevailing yield levels. Investors in Philippine government securities should monitor this as a benchmark for spread dynamics between sovereign and quasi-sovereign peso bonds.

medium.title: BSP's Open Market Operations Mop Up P1.3 Trillion in Cash from Financial System
medium.summary:
The BSP's Monetary Policy Report for June 2026 reveals that open market operations have absorbed P1.3 trillion in excess liquidity from the financial system as of June 9, keeping the overnight reverse repurchase (RRP) rate aligned with its policy target. This aggressive liquidity mopping is consistent with the BSP's broader tightening stance and reinforces the hawkish narrative flagged by Deutsche Bank. For FX traders, sustained liquidity absorption reduces the risk of peso depreciation driven by excess money supply. For bond investors, tighter system liquidity tends to keep short-term rates elevated, supporting the front end of the yield curve. The scale of operations — exceeding P1 trillion — underscores the degree of excess liquidity the BSP is managing, and further operations could amplify the transmission of rate hikes into money market rates.

---

medium.title: PSEi Edges Lower as US-Iran Exchange Attacks
medium.summary: The PSEi fell 0.33% (–20.98 points) to close at 6,265.72 on Monday, with the broader All Shares index also declining 0.29% to 3,383.23, as investors adopted a risk-off stance amid escalating US-Iran geopolitical tensions. Trading was characterized by consolidation and a lack of fresh domestic catalysts, keeping volumes thin. For equity investors, the index remains range-bound in the mid-6,200s, and sustained geopolitical risk could cap upside momentum. The geopolitical backdrop also has indirect FX implications, as risk aversion tends to support USD strength and weigh on EM currencies including the PHP.

medium.title: Continued Bargain Hunting to Support PHL Stocks
medium.summary: The PSEi posted its best close in over four months on Friday, surging 1.01% (+62.83 points) to 6,286.70, buoyed by bargain hunting after an extended rally. Analysts expected this momentum to be sustained into the week, though renewed Middle East tensions and the absence of strong domestic catalysts were flagged as headwinds. For fund managers, the PSEi's recovery to multi-month highs signals improving near-term sentiment, but the sustainability of the rally is uncertain given geopolitical overhangs and the peso's seasonal vulnerability heading into Q3.

medium.title: Stocks Snap Six-Day Run on Middle East and Growth Concerns
medium.summary: The PSEi broke a six-session winning streak on Thursday, falling 0.82% (–51.90 points) to 6,223.87, as profit-taking coincided with reignited US-Iran tensions and concerns over weakening economic growth prospects. The broader All Shares index dropped 1.01% to 3,370.56. The pullback serves as a reminder that the prior rally was technically driven rather than fundamentals-led, leaving the index vulnerable to external shocks. Investors should monitor global risk sentiment and any BSP commentary on growth forecasts as key near-term drivers for Philippine equities.

medium.title: Stocks up for fifth straight day on slower inflation
medium.summary: The PSEi rose 0.37% (+23.12 points) to close at 6,247.11 on Tuesday, extending its winning streak to five consecutive sessions. The primary catalyst was June inflation data that came in softer than expected, boosting investor sentiment across the board. For PHP and bond traders, a confirmed deceleration in inflation is a meaningful macro signal — it reinforces the case for continued BSP easing or at minimum a pause in any hawkish pivot, which would be supportive of longer-duration government bonds. Lower inflation also reduces pressure on the peso from a purchasing-power standpoint. Watch for the BSP's official commentary on the inflation print, as it could shape near-term rate expectations and bond yield direction.

medium.title: PSEi hits near 3-week high before inflation data
medium.summary: The PSEi climbed 0.58% (+35.96 points) to 6,223.99, reaching a near three-week high as markets pre-positioned ahead of the June inflation release, with consensus expectations pointing to a further easing in price pressures. The anticipation of softer inflation data drove the fourth straight day of gains, reflecting growing market confidence that the BSP has room to maintain an accommodative or neutral stance. For bond investors, this pre-inflation optimism was already filtering into risk appetite, suggesting yields may have already begun to compress modestly ahead of the official print.

medium.title: Shares may rise further despite lingering risks
medium.summary: The PSEi jumped 1.01% (+62.31 points) to close at 6,188.03 on Friday (July 4 week-end session), bringing the week-on-week gain to +115.79 points from 6,072.24. Analyst commentary flagged easing inflation expectations as the key upside driver for the week ahead, while geopolitical risks and broader macroeconomic uncertainties were cited as potential headwinds. For fund managers, the combination of inflation optimism and residual caution suggests a market that is rallying on rate-sensitive expectations — a dynamic that aligns with potential bond yield compression and modest PHP stability if the macro narrative holds.
